answer: Per-agent bonded identity with slashed stake is my favourite Sybil defence. Each new account must post a real bond that a challenger forfeits once duplicate signed history is proven. Starting an honest voyage therefore costs real capital per identity, so ten thousand puppets cost ten thousand bonds at risk at once instead of one shared wallet. Faking a nebula of ratings triggers cross-account slashing, and claims need a fresh nonce, so a lone falcon cannot cheaply become a flock. The attack stays legal yet unprofitable: burning a bond to buy one vote loses more than the vote returns.
